To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the precipitated lignin fractions obtained from silver birchesoda-anthraquinon black liquor by carbonization and/or acidification are chemically very similar.

the precipitated lignin from silver birch black liquor was found to be a mixture of softwood-like and hardwood-like lignins, and its chemical structure and molecular weight distribution were not affected by the precipitation conditions.

the lignin fractions obtained by selective acidification of the carbonated soda-AQ black liquor were characterized by a similar chemical composition to the lignin fractions recovered from the carbonated soda-Anthraquinone (AQ) black liquor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recovery of lignin from black liquor, a potential source of lignin.
the characterization of hardwood soda-AQ lignin fractions obtained from black liquor.
the development of new integrated biorefining processes for the production of value-added products from black liquors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lignins precipitated by selective acidification from soda-anthraquine black liquor can be utilized as a raw material in the same way as the carbonated lignins.
the acidification process is a promising alternative to the carbonation process for precipitating hardwood soda-AQ lignin from black liquor.
the precipitated lignin fractions from silver birch soda-anthraquionone black liquor were very similar, regardless of the precipitation conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the recovery of lignin from black liquors, acidification with H2SO(4) is an alternative to the carbonation process, but the latter is more suitable when the lignin is to be used in the production of carbon fibers.
, in the case of soda-AQ black liquors, lignin can be selectively precipitated from the liquors at pH 8.5 or 2 by carbonation or acidification, respectively.

the selective acidification of black liquors is a feasible and efficient method for the recovery of lignins, but the lignin fractions obtained from this process need to be further purified before their chemical utilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the precipitated lignin fractions from silver birch soda-anthraquine black liquor can be used in the same way as commercial hardwood kraft lignin.
lignins can be recovered from sulfur-free black liquors by selective acidification with H2SO 4, which can also be used for the precipitation.
the precipitated lignin fractions from black liquor are chemically similar, and therefore, their equal chemical use is possible.
